Name: modular_tanb77_adjuvant_platform
Title: A Modular Platform Combining Engineered TANB77 Colonization and Pilin-Mimetic Nanoparticles for Personalized Enhancement of Immune Checkpoint Blockade
Experiment: We will conduct a multi-phase preclinical study integrating in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. (1) Datasets: Use the original ten ICB patient cohorts (metagenomes and response data) plus two newly recruited prospective cohorts (n=200 each, mixed NSCLC and melanoma) with deep immune phenotyping. For mechanistic studies, generate single-cell RNA-seq and CyTOF data from mouse tumors and gut-associated lymphoid tissues. (2) Metrics: Primary endpoint in mouse models is tumor volume inhibition; secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, intratumoral CD8+ T-cell density, serum pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-12, IFN-γ), gut TANB77 abundance by qPCR, and TLR4 downstream signaling markers (NF-κB, IRF3 phosphorylation). In human cohorts, correlate TANB77 colonization with RECIST response, microbiome diversity, and circulating immune cell profiles. (3) Baseline comparisons: Six-arm mouse experiment: (i) isotype control + PBS, (ii) anti-PD-1 alone, (iii) anti-PD-1 + wild-type TANB77 oral gavage, (iv) anti-PD-1 + TANB77Δpilin mutant (genetically deleted pilin-like protein), (v) anti-PD-1 + pilin-mimetic lipid nanoparticles (oral), (vi) anti-PD-1 + TANB77Δpilin + pilin nanoparticles. A seventh arm tests anti-CTLA-4 synergy. Each arm has n=15 mice. (4) Expected outcomes: The dual-module therapy (arm vi) will achieve the highest response rate due to colonization-mediated ecological niche modulation and nanoparticle-driven dendritic cell activation, mimicking natural pilin-TLR4 signaling without live bacterial dependency. We expect that TANB77Δpilin alone is ineffective, confirming pilin necessity, while pilin nanoparticles alone provide partial benefit via systemic immune priming. The human cohorts will reveal that baseline TANB77 abundance predicts response only when combined with a defined immune signature, enabling patient stratification. (5) Ablation studies: Test pilin nanoparticles with different multimerization states (monomer, dimer, trimer) to determine the minimal active unit; use conditional TLR4-knockout dendritic cell mice to validate target specificity; vary the ratio of live bacteria to nanoparticles in co-administration to map dose-response synergy; and use faecal microbiota transplantation from TANB77-colonized to germ-free mice to isolate colonization effects from pre-existing microbiota interactions.
